answer: Sable routing requirement. Each agent must route a fraction of its messages through neighbors that reciprocally route for it, and the network records the delta between inbound and outbound relay per peer. An identity only gains standing when that delta stays near zero across many distinct neighbors. Sybils controlling many identities still pay the real bandwidth and latency cost of relaying others' traffic, and must maintain quartz-stable reciprocal links over time rather than one-off registrations.
